headline: The dollar remains strong overall, but eased back a touch today, giving the euro a small bounce.
summary: Markets had been pricing in the chance of another Fed rate hike as well as concern that France's fiscal and political troubles would keep weighing on the euro. What actually happened: the Fed's September meeting minutes, released Thursday, showed many officials favor just one more hike this year rather than the multiple hikes traders had been expecting, while France's budget worries and widening French-German bond yields have continued to pressure the euro this week. The net effect: EUR/USD edged up to around 1.1200 on Thursday after the euro came close to a 17-month low near 1.1160 earlier in the week, though the euro is still down noticeably over the past month.

whatMattersNext.label: US weekly jobless claims report and several Fed officials speaking

forYou: The dollar is still relatively strong versus the euro by recent-month standards, so converting USD to EUR is a bit more favorable than it's been for a while, even though the euro ticked up slightly today.
